items.title: Service case stemming from ₹67: Delhi HC slaps ₹1 lakh costs on DTC for 32-year-old litigation against conductor
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has imposed costs of ₹1 lakh on Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC) for pursuing a case for 32 years against a conductor's claim for 17 months' back wages [ DTC vs Rajender Prashad ]. The case itself stemmed from the conductor's dismissal for allegedly taking ₹67 from passengers without issuing tickets to them. In the judgment delivered on September 2, Justice Amit Mahajan observed that the prolonged dispute resulted in abuse of the process of law and avoidable expenditure of public money. Hence, it refused to entertain the petition filed by DTC challenging a 2004 award passed by the Industrial Tribunal, which had allowed the conductor’s claim for back wages. “The continued litigation over such a limited claim, for an inordinately long period, amounts to an abuse of the process of law and has resulted in avoidable expenditure of public money,” the Court stated. Justice Amit Mahajan, Delhi High Court The industrial dispute dating back to 1994, pertained to DTC’s action against its bus conductor, Rajender Prashad, for allegedly taking ₹67 from the passengers without issuing tickets to them. Disciplinary proceedings were initiated against Parshad and he was subsequently removed from service in 1996. On Parshad’s appeal to the Managing Director of DTC, he was reinstated without back wages. Parshad then raised an industrial dispute against the denial of back wages. The Industrial Tribunal allowed his plea, observing that the punishment awarded was illegal and baseless. It directed DTC to pay arrears of wages for the two-year period between 1996 and 1998. DTC moved the High Court challenging the Tribunal’s award. In 2005, the Court stayed the operation of the award. In the final verdict delivered on September 2, the Court upheld the Industrial Tribunal’s decision as reasonable and plausible. It observed that the manner in which DTC pursued the litigation, warrants imposition of costs on its officers. Thus, it imposed costs of ₹1 lakh, out of which ₹25,000 will have to be paid to the Delhi High Court Legal Services Committee, ₹50,000 to the Prime Minister Relief Fund and the remaining ₹25,000 to Parshad. The Court also granted liberty to DTC to recover the costs from the officer responsible for pursuing such “insignificant dispute." Advocate Manisha Tyagi appeared for DTC. Advocates Rishabh Verma and Anil Aggarwal appeared for Parshad. [Read Judgment]

items.title: RSS not a political party: Karnataka tribunal stays teacher's suspension for attending RSS event
items.summary: The Karnataka State Administrative Tribunal (KSAT) at Kalburgi has stayed the suspension of a government school teacher who participated in a Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) event [Gururaj v. State of Karnataka]. A coram of Judicial Member SY Watawati and Administrative Member Dr Amita Prasad said that the school teacher had not violated the Karnataka State Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 2021 that prevents government servants from attending functions organised by political parties or by associations that participate in politics. The Tribunal further held the applicant had not violated any State government order or notification that explicitly barred participation in events. It further held the RSS to be a non-political party. "When he participated in the event organized by a non-political party, the act of the applicant did not violate the conditions stipulated under Rule 5 of the Conduct Rules, 2021 referred to supra. Further, the State Government has not issued any order or notification prohibiting any Government Official from participating in such an event." S Y Watawati, Dr Amita Prasad The applicant was an assistant teacher at Government Girls High School, Hunasagi. On August 20, 2026, the Deputy Director of the Department of School Education, Yadgiri, placed him under suspension for having participated in RSS events and activities. Gururaj did not dispute that he had participated in an RSS function, but contended that there was no bar on participation in a programme of a non-political organisation. It also pointed out that Rule 7, which had been cited in the suspension order, had been omitted from the Conduct Rules since April 25, 1968. Advocate MM Sangond appeared for Gururaj. Additional Government Advocate Viranagouda M Biradar appeared for the State and Department of School Education. [Read order]

items.title: Allahabad HC flags judge’s bail order in dowry death case, suggests inquiry
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court has asked its administrative side to consider whether an inquiry is needed against a trial judge for arbitrarily granting bail to a man in a dowry death case [Smt Seema Devi v State of UP and Another] Justice Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal noted that when Additional Sessions Judge Satish Chandra Dwivedi was asked to explain how he had granted bail to the victim’s husband, even he could not justify his decision. Thus, the Court said there was “suspicion” in the exercise of the trial judge’s discretion as the bail order was passed without any reason. However, it declined to express any view on the integrity of the trial judge and referred the matter to its administrative side. “Therefore, matter be placed before the Administrative Committee to consider whether any enquiry is required to be conducted against Sri Satish Chandra Dwivedi, learned Additional Sessions Judge, Court, No.1, Jalaun at Orai, regarding such erroneous and arbitrary exercise of power while releasing the opposite party no.2 (husband of the deceased) on bail despite sufficient material against him which attracts the presumption u/s 118 of BSA,” Justice Deshwal said. Justice Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal The Court passed the order while dealing with an application seeking cancellation of the bail granted to the accused in the case registered last year at Sirsakalaar police Station in Jalaun district. It was argued that the trial court had failed to consider that the victim had died within seven years of marriage under unnatural circumstances and that there was evidence to show that soon before her death, she was subjected to cruelty for dowry. In July, the High Court asked the trial judge to submit his explanation in the matter. The trial court judge conceded that there was evidence of harassment in the case but explained that he had granted bail on the ground of parity with the parents of the accused. When the matter was taken up on September 1, Justice Deshwal opined that the discretion of bail was arbitrarily exercised by the trial court judge and proceeded to cancel the bail order. The Court directed the accused to surrender within 10 days. Advocate Shahbaz Khan represented the petitioner. Advocate Deepak Kumar Verma represented the accused. Additional Government Advocate Roshan Kumar Singh represented the State. [Read Order]

items.title: Delhi HC refuses to reject Canada’s suit to recover 33.3 million allegedly siphoned to India by ex-bureaucrat
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has refused to reject a suit filed by the Government of Canada seeking recovery of over CAD 33.3 million allegedly siphoned from the Government of Ontario into bank accounts in India [Government of Canada Vs Sanjay Madan] Justice Vikas Mahajan ruled that the Delhi High Court has the territorial jurisdiction to hear the suit since the funds allegedly misappropriated were transferred to bank accounts maintained in Delhi. The Court rejected the argument that Canada was the more appropriate forum to adjudicate the dispute. Justice Vikas Mahajan The suit filed by Canadian government arises from two fraud schemes involving former Ontario government employee Sanjay Madan. According to the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation , Madan had a senior IT role and helped develop a computer application related to a COVID-19 relief benefit before he was fired in 2020. Madan pleaded guilty before the Ontario Superior Court of Justice in April 2023 to criminal charges concerning fraud on the Ontario government and admitted receiving secret commissions or kickbacks between 2011 and 2020, the High Court was told. items.title: Supreme Court’s recent arbitration rulings have created grave uncertainty: Retired Justice Rohinton Nariman
items.summary: Former Supreme Court Justice Rohinton F Nariman recently said that some of the Supreme Court’s recent arbitration judgments were incorrect and had created “grave uncertainty” by reopening settled questions. Justice Nariman was delivering the keynote address at the Gujarat High Court Arbitration Centre’s Arbitration Week 2026. He examined 5 recent Constitution Bench decisions concerning the appointment of arbitrators and challenges to arbitral awards. “ Here we have five recent judgments of the Supreme Court. How has the Act fared? According to me, not particularly well, because, firstly, the judgments don’t conduce to certainty . Secondly, constantly reopening closed questions again leads to grave uncertainty. Some of the judgments, unfortunately, are on the face of them not correct, in my humble submission .” Justice Nariman first referred to the five-judge ruling in Cox and Kings . The judgment held that the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 had to be read with the Contract Act while deciding whether a non-signatory intended to be bound by an arbitration agreement. He contrasted this with the subsequent 7-judge ruling on unstamped arbitration agreements. That judgment described the Arbitration Act as a self-contained code and special enactment. Justice Nariman said that this reasoning contradicted Cox and Kings , where the Contract Act had been treated as fundamental to determining the existence of an arbitration agreement. He also criticised the speed with which the earlier 5-judge ruling in NN Global was reopened by a seven-judge bench. He said, “ Unfortunately, what was made certain by 5 judges was made uncertain. God alone knows now whether a 9-judge bench will overrule this view, or whether whatever happens, happens .” Justice Nariman then criticised the Supreme Court’s curative judgment in the Delhi Metro dispute. The Court had set aside an arbitral award in favour of Delhi Airport Metro Express Private Limited (DAMEPL) after finding that the judgment upholding it had resulted in a miscarriage of justice. items.title: Mar Thoma priest calls for mandatory HIV tests before marriages, sparks controversy
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A senior priest of the Mar Thoma Church has sparked a controversy by suggesting that HIV tests should be made mandatory before marriages are solemnised in their church. In the same speech, Mar Thoma Church Clergy Trustee Rev. Dr K Thomas advised parents to ensure that their daughters’ bodies had not been “abused” before marriage, appearing to refer to sexual intercourse. The remarks were made at a Mar Thoma gathering in Thiruvananthapuram on August 30. Thomas began his speech by recounting the case of a 17-year-old girl who was in a romantic relationship and whose family had approached him for counselling. He then spoke about the issue in the context of his counselling experience. “The Karnataka government is now conducting HIV tests on all the campuses there. Let me say this, I am someone who believes that all marriages that take place in the Mar Thoma Church should be conducted only after the individuals have undergone such tests,” he said. However, the claim that Karnataka is conducting HIV tests on all college campuses is incorrect. The Karnataka State AIDS Prevention Society (KSAPS) clarified in the last week of July that HIV testing had not been made mandatory for college students. The clarification came after reports claimed that 7,000 students in the state had tested positive for HIV. Thomas later addressed parents of girls and said they should be able to ensure that their daughters had not been “abused” before marriage. “Parents, please don't misunderstand me. I am only reminding you of a word of instruction. Do you know what the responsibility of a father and mother is? When a 27-year-old girl is brought into the church as a bride, the father and mother should be able to assure that her body has not been abused,” he said. The speech drew criticism after Malayalam news channels aired excerpts, with several people describing his remarks as regressive and patriarchal. Speaking to Asianet News, Thomas defended his remarks and said he was addressing parents in the context of the situation in Karnataka. “There were around a thousand parents in front of me. They need to have this awareness because we are facing such a major challenge. I wasn't addressing the youth directly. I was speaking in the context of Karnataka,” he said.

items.title: Bengaluru DEO admits voters were wrongly flagged, says they must still face inquiry
items.summary: The Bengaluru Urban district election office has admitted that some voters in the Byatarayanapura Assembly constituency were wrongly marked as having “No mapping” despite having correct records in the 2002 electoral roll. The office, however, said these voters will still have to undergo an inquiry by election officials. According to a press note issued on Wednesday, September 2, the Election Registration Officer (ERO) and Assistant Electoral Registration Officer (AERO) will examine such cases, collect documents from the concerned voters and verify their eligibility. The Additional District Election Officer (ADEO) will subsequently ensure that eligible voters are included in the final electoral roll. The admission came after reports alleged irregularities in the digitisation and mapping of voter samples during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in the 152-Byatarayanapura constituency. The district election office said it scrutinised several polling booths in the constituency, including booths 158, 284, 206, 161, 163, 167, 168, 176 and 177. Detailed scrutiny was carried out at booths 206, 176 and 177. At booth 206, which has 1,249 voters, 722 voter samples had been digitised. Of these, 488 were marked as “No mapping”. The election office said 434 had no corresponding record in the 2002 SIR electoral roll, while 51 had incomplete or mismatched details. However, three voters had correct records in the 2002 electoral roll but had still been wrongly marked as “No mapping”, the office acknowledged. At booth 176, there were 1,349 voters, of whom 866 samples had been digitised. Ninety-two were marked “No mapping”. The office said 85 had no corresponding 2002 record and seven had mismatched details. No cases were found where a voter with a correct 2002 record had been wrongly marked. At booth 177, out of 1,388 voters, 778 samples had been digitised, and 113 were marked “No mapping”. Of these, 104 had no corresponding 2002 record, and nine had mismatched details. Again, the office said no voters with correct 2002 records had been wrongly marked. The election office said the majority of “No mapping” cases were due to the absence of corresponding records in the old electoral roll or discrepancies in the available details, rather than errors in the digitisation process. However, even where voters were wrongly marked as “No mapping”, the concerned ERO and AERO will conduct an inquiry, the press note said. The officials will collect documents

items.title: HarperCollins steps in to publish Sonia Gandhi memoir Belonging after Penguin fallout
items.summary: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi’s upcoming memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love , has found a new publisher in HarperCollins India after a sudden fallout with Penguin Random House India over editorial differences. HarperCollins announced on Friday, September 4, that it will publish the book on November 10, 2026. The development comes days after Penguin Random House India (PRHI) pulled back from releasing the title, citing an impasse over "a particular issue" during the editing process. The book was originally announced in mid-August by US publisher Alfred A. Knopf as a global release, with PRHI handling the Indian edition and planning a print run of 100,000 copies. However, negotiations stalled during editorial review. News reports, citing sources, indicated that differences arose over political commentary in the manuscript, including Sonia Gandhi’s observations about Prime Minister Narendra Modi during official meetings, her thoughts on being called certain derogatory names by Modi during campaigning, her perspective on India-China relations, and her views on the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS). The fallout sparked sharp political debate. Congress leaders, including Ashok Gehlot and Kamal Nath, alleged that PRHI gave in to government pressure to edit sensitive sections. PRHI spokesperson Pallavi Narayan strongly denied these claims, stating that because the embargoed manuscript was handled under strict confidentiality, there was "no external pressure whatsoever." PRHI maintained that while changes were agreed upon on several points, the parties could not reach an understanding on one final issue, leading Gandhi’s team to withdraw from the contract. HarperCollins India stepped in shortly after to acquire the publishing rights without requesting content changes. In its official announcement, the publisher described the memoir as a riveting account that "seamlessly weaves the personal with the political." The book promises a candid look into Sonia Gandhi’s early childhood in post-war Italy, her romance with Rajiv Gandhi, and the personal tragedies that reshaped her life and thrust her into Indian politics. The memoir remains one of the year’s most anticipated political releases, offering an inside account of modern Indian history from one of the country's most reticent leaders.

items.title: CM Vijay announces new secretariat building at estimated cost of Rs 1200 crore
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay announced plans to construct an integrated Assembly and Secretariat complex on Thursday, September 3. The new building is planned to be built across 20 lakh square feet with an estimated cost of Rs 1,200 crore. The integrated complex will house the Legislative Assembly, the offices of the chief minister and other ministers, and other government departments. Announcing the plans in the Assembly, Chief Minister Vijay said that the present buildings at the Fort St George campus cannot be expanded further because of limited land availability. The newly proposed complex is touted to meet all administrative requirements of the next 100 years. This includes modern infrastructure, parking facilities, conference halls, and public service centres. The location of the proposed complex has not been announced. The proposal comes after several previous attempts to move the Assembly and Secretariat buildings. In 2010, former chief minister M Karunanidhi shifted the Assembly and Secretariat to a newly constructed building at Omandurar Government Estate. However, it was shifted back to the Fort St George building in 2011 when J Jayalalitha came to power. The building in Omandurar was converted into a hospital. This story was written by a student interning with TNM .
